chunks.page_content: The Freemium business model has been in use by the software industry since the 1980s. In the Freemium pricing strategy, money (premium) is charged for additional features, services, or virtual goods. In the Freemium pricing strategy, a product or service is provided free of charge. The product or service in the Freemium pricing strategy is typically a digital offering or application such as software, media, games or web services. The Freemium business model has been used as a licensing scheme by the software industry since the 1980s. "Freemium" is a portmanteau of "free" and "premium". A subset of the Freemium model used by the video gaming industry is called free-to-play. Freemium is a pricing strategy.

chunks.chunk_summary: This chunk contains information about the definition, permissions, user benefits, cost characteristics, licensing criteria, and potential restrictions of open-source licenses for software and other products.
chunks.page_content: An open-source license allows the source code, blueprint or design to be used, modified and/or shared under defined terms and conditions. Open-source licensed software is mostly available free of charge. Open-source licensed software does not necessarily have to be available free of charge. A license that requires redistribution of the licensed software only under the same license is known as a copyleft license. Open-source licenses may have restrictions regarding the expression of respect to the origin of software. An open-source license allows end users and commercial companies to review and modify the source code, blueprint or design for their own customization, curiosity or troubleshooting needs. Some open-source licenses have a requirement to preserve the name of the authors within the code. Some open-source licenses have a requirement to preserve a copyright statement within the code. Open-source licenses may have some restrictions. The Open Source Initiative (OSI) approves licenses based on their Open Source Definition (OSD). Licenses which only permit non-commercial redistribution or modification of the source code for personal use only are generally not considered as open-source licenses. An open-source license is a type of license for computer software and other products. Some open-source licenses have a requirement to redistribute the licensed software only under the same license. One popular set of open-source software licenses are those approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
